dedupe_keys.name: synthetic mobile money transaction dataset momtsim

description: This dataset holds labelled synthetic mobile money transactions generated with MoMTSim, a multi-agent simulation platform built and calibrated at Makerere University in Kampala, Uganda, to emulate the mobile money ecosystem of clients, banks, merchants and fraudsters. Each record has a time step, amount, initial and new balances of initiator and recipient, participant identifiers, the transaction type (deposit, withdrawal, transfer, payment or debit) and a label for legitimate or fraudulent, covering fraud typologies such as account takeover through SIM swaps and lost credentials, refund fraud and sharing of personal identifiers. Simulation rules and probabilities were derived from a large real transaction dataset, and fidelity was checked with sum of squared errors, Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests and Bland-Altman plots. The CSV files are on Mendeley Data (version 2, issued 29 October 2024) under CC-BY-4.0, described in a Data in Brief article and in an IEEE Access paper on MoMTSim. Coverage is an East African style mobile money system, not one country's records. Caveats: the data are synthetic, and fraud rates and behaviours reflect the model's calibration. For simulation it supports agent-based and fraud or disruption scenarios in mobile money systems that many households depend on. Related catalogue records include the Global Findex Database and the Carnegie cyber incident timeline.
